title: Session binding mismatch during node drain leads to transient org misbinding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple Dedicated customers reported a short window (10-30s) during planned node drains where API requests authenticated with recently rotated signed API keys were accepted against the wrong tenant binding. Symptoms: customers saw requests from service-side integrations return 403 for their own org then suddenly succeed with a different org's data returned in logs. This surfaced during a controlled capacity rebalance where node drain + KV cache eviction + key rotation overlapped.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Dedicated pool with node drain enabled and short graceful drain (30s).
2) Enable signed API key rotation on the customer org with rotation TTL 60s and immediate issuance of new signatures,
3) Flood the node with concurrent long-lived chat generation requests that use KV cache lookups and prefix caching,
4) Trigger a drain of the node serving those sessions, and observe request logs across the next 60s for tenant binding anomalies.
investigation_notes: 2025-03-10 - Marcus: Reproduced locally with a synthetic harness. Race occurs when (a) the old API key record is removed from the per-node signed-key cache, (b) a rolling refresh of the session binding map queries the global store and gets a partially-applied update, and (c) an in-flight request uses a transient fast-path that checks node-local KV before global validation.

Root cause: ordering mismatch between cache eviction and session binding refresh under drain. The node fast-path did a permissive fallback when lookup failed which allowed an accept + later reconciliation wrote the request's tenant into audit logs for a different org. Not a complete ACL bypass, but allowed short-lived mapping ambiguity leading to logs / routing showing wrong tenant.

Impact vector: Dedicated customers with very short rotation windows or aggressive drain settings are most affected; Hosted customers are low-risk because central control-plane prevents overlapping operations during rotations. Private deployments with asynchronous key sync may be exposed depending on upgrade timing.
fix: Patch: 1) Make local signed-key eviction atomic with session-binding refresh by introducing a per-node drain token and sequencing guard. 2) Remove permissive fast-path fallback: on cache-miss during drain, reject and fallback to synchronous global validation rather than optimistic accept. 3) Add additional telemetry to detect transient tenant-binding mismatches.
Unit tests: added deterministic harness for drain+rotation race, integration test targeting Dedicated pool with simulated key rotation.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy runtime-2.3.1 candidate to 5% of Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 with drain token feature flag enabled.
Smoke: run synthetic harness and run the 'drain rotation' regression test 1000 iterations within cluster; monitor tenant-binding mismatch metric.
Gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h with manual holdpoints and customer communication for impacted accounts.
Rollback: roll back to runtime-2.3.0 if tenant-binding-mismatch rate > 0.01% of auth flow or any confirmed customer data exposure reported.
Private: produce patch bundle for on-prem customers and coordinate with Solutions for out-of-band upgrades; provide migration instructions and hotfix script.
follow_up_tasks: Post-mortem and RCA write-up in Confluence (owner: Aisha).
Add end-to-end telemetry that correlates API key rotation events, node drain tokens, and request tenant assignment (owner: Observability team).
Provide a mitigation script for customers: temporarily increase rotation TTL and increase drain grace period until upgrades applied (owner: Solutions).
Audit: run a 7-day retrospective on other places with optimistic fast-paths to ensure no similar permissive behavior (owner: Security).
